chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the woman in Ihram, 'What of the clothes can she wear?' He said: 'She can wear all clothes, except those dyed with saffron and the dye plant (wars); and she cannot wear the two gloves, nor an ornament with which she adorns herself for her husband; and she cannot apply kohl except due to a reason; and she cannot touch perfume; and she cannot wear an ornament, nor Firanda (a decorative flower); and there is no problem with a pattern in the clothes.'

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُحْرِمَةِ: The woman in the state of Ihram
key_terms.فِرِنْداً: Firanda (a type of decorative flower or fabric)

ai.seo_question: What clothes and accessories can a woman wear while in the state of Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the attire for women in Ihram, distinguishing between garments dyed with saffron or wars (which are prohibited due to their distinctiveness and fragrance) and those with simple patterns or 'Alam' (permissible). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on modesty and the removal of adornment, ensuring the pilgrim's focus remains on spiritual devotion rather than worldly beauty. The prohibition of gloves and specific ornaments underscores the uniformity of the pilgrim's state, mirroring the male prohibition on head coverings.
